Difference in Kaplan–Meier survival at a fixed time point

Source: R/OncReg.survival.R
OR.KMdiff.Rd

Compares Kaplan–Meier survival at a fixed time point between each arm and the baseline arm (the lowest value of group). Confidence intervals use unpooled Greenwood¹ variances on the identity scale and p-values use Wald tests on the complementary log–log scale².

Usage

OR.KMdiff(time, status, group, fixedt, conf.level = 0.95, LOCF = FALSE)

Arguments

time

Numeric vector of follow-up times.

status

Numeric vector of event indicators, where 1 denotes the event and 0 denotes censoring.

group

Numeric vector of arm indicators. The lowest value is the baseline arm.

fixedt

Numeric time point at which survival is compared.

conf.level

Numeric confidence level. Default = 0.95.

LOCF

Logical. If TRUE, survival beyond an arm's last observation is carried forward³. If FALSE, it is NA unless the Kaplan–Meier estimate has reached 0. Default = FALSE.

Value

A numeric matrix with one row per non-baseline arm, named by its group value, and columns:

diff

Survival difference, arm minus baseline.

SE

Standard error of the difference.

LL

Lower confidence limit.

UL

Upper confidence limit.

p

Two-sided p-value.

Details

Where survival reaches 0, the standard error is set to 0 (whereas survival::survfit() returns NaN). This keeps results usable in downstream pooling (e.g., multiple imputation), where a single NaN would propagate to the pooled estimate. When either arm's survival is 0 or 1, the complementary log–log transform is undefined and the p-value falls back to the identity-scale Wald test. When both standard errors are 0, the p-value is 1 if the arms are equal and 0 otherwise.

References

  1. Greenwood, M., 1926. A report on the natural duration of cancer. In: Reports on Public Health and Medical Subjects, 33, pp. 1–26. London: Her Majesty’s Stationery Office, Ministry of Health.

  2. Klein, J.P., Logan, B., Harhoff, M. and Andersen, P.K., 2007. Analyzing survival curves at a fixed point in time. Statistics in Medicine, 26(24), pp. 4505–4519.

  3. Gill, R.D., 1983. Large sample behaviour of the product-limit estimator on the whole line. The Annals of Statistics, 11(1), pp. 49–58.

See also
